title: 3D biomimetic environment enabling ex utero trophoblast invasion and co-culture of embryos and somatic cells
protocol: Inject intraperitoneally female mice with 100 μL of PMSG (100 U/mL).
After 48 h, administer 100 μL of HCG (100 U/mL) via intraperitoneal injection and set up mating with stud males.
Check for a vaginal plug the next day.
Humanely euthanize the pregnant mice at day three and a half post coitum.
Cut through the skin and peritoneum to locate the reproductive tract.
Collect the uteri together with the oviduct and ovaries in prewarmed M2 medium.
Under a stereomicroscope, cut off the ovary and the oviduct using spring scissors.
Fill a syringe with prewarmed M2 medium and attach the needle.
Place the needle into the uterine horn and flush the lumen with M2 medium at least 3 times.
Flush also the connection between the uterus and the oviduct to ensure that all embryos are released.
Collect and transfer the blastocysts into a 4-well plate filled with prewarmed M2 medium using mouth pipetting.
Invert the lid of a 35 mm dish and place 30 μL drops of prewarmed Tyrode’s solution and 30 μL drops of prewarmed M2 medium.
Transfer small groups of 10–20 embryos from the 4-well plate into a drop of M2 medium.
Remove the remaining medium from the mouth pipette and aspirate Tyrode’s solution.
Transfer the embryos into Tyrode’s solution drop.
Expunge the remaining liquid and refill the pipette with fresh Tyrode’s solution.
Transfer the embryos into the second drop of Tyrode’s solution.
Repeat this one more time and observe the quick disappearance of Zona pellucida (within 30 s) in the third drop of Tyrode’s solution.
Fill the pipette with medium.
Immediately transfer the Zona-free blastocysts into a drop of M2 medium.
Expunge the remaining liquid.
Refill the pipette with fresh M2 medium.
Repeat this step one more time and transfer the embryos to a 4-well plate filled with prewarmed M2 medium.
Observe carefully the embryos for any remaining zona pellucida.
If necessary, repeat steps 4 to 6 to ensure complete removal of the zona pellucida.
Culture E3.5 blastocysts in IVC1 medium for 24 h if natural hatching is preferred.
Transfer embryos from M2 medium to IVC1 medium.
Pipette 1 ml of IVC1 medium into each well of a 4-well plate.
Place the plate into a humidified incubator with an atmosphere of 5% CO2 at 37°C for 30 min.
Culture blastocysts in IVC1 medium for 16-20 h.
Prepare PEG or DexMA hydrogel solution as specified.
Pipette 10 μl of the hydrogel solution into the inner well of a μ-slide 3D.
Transfer 5–10 blastocysts into the PEG/DexMA hydrogel solution.
Place the embryos at an equal distance from each other.
Maintain the embryos in the middle of the hydrogel depth by sequential mouth pipetting while the PEG/DexMA solution gradually increases its viscosity.
Transfer the embryos from the IVC1 medium to the hydrogel solution using as little medium as possible to avoid diluting the hydrogel solution.
Ensure the blastocysts are completely embedded in the hydrogel.
Adjust the position of the embryos at the fourth minute after pipetting if necessary.
Place the μ-slide in a humidified incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 15 minutes.
Allow the hydrogel to polymerize completely.
Pipette 40 μL of IVC2 medium into the upper chamber of the well.
Add 10 μL mineral oil to prevent evaporation of the medium.
Culture the embryos in a humidified incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Equilibrate the temperature and pH of the IVC2 medium at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 30 minutes before adding it to the μ-slide.
Observe the embryo development.
Isolate blastocysts from superovulated females.
Remove Zona pellucida from isolated blastocysts.
Culture embryos in IVC1 medium for 16-20 hours in a 4-well plate.
Prepare the DexMA hydrogel as per instructions.
Assemble the microfluidic device as described.
Store assembled microfluidic chip at 4°C to prevent gelatin coating melting.
Position embryos in the reservoir containing DexMA hydrogel.
Pipette 65 μL of the DexMA hydrogel solution into the middle reservoir of the device.
Transfer 5–7 embryos into the hydrogel.
Position the embryos in close proximity of 100–150 μm to the channel.
Maintain the position of the embryos for approximately 5 min by mouth pipetting, while the hydrogel polymerizes.
Place the device in a humidified chamber at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 30 min allowing the hydrogel to polymerize completely.
Add 500 μL of IVC2 medium on top of the device covering the hydrogel chamber and the 4 reservoirs.
Place the device in a 100 mm Petri dish containing wet paper to the side.
Place the device in a humidified incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Incubate overnight.
Place the device in a tissue culture hood.
Carefully pull the needles out using forceps.
Hold the device using another forceps while pulling.
Keep the pulling direction straight to prevent damaging the channels by the tip of the needle.
Ensure that the reservoirs of the device are filled with IVC2 medium.
Place some medium on top of the device.
As the needles are pulled out, let the medium flow from the reservoirs into the channels.
Refill the reservoirs as medium flows in from the top surface of the device.
Seal the open ends where the needles were inserted using vacuum grease.
Remove any excess medium from the surface of the sealed device carefully.
Absorb any traces of medium from the bottom surface using filter paper.
Place the device on a 100 mm plate coated with PDMS.
Ensure that the device has adhered well to the PDMS.
Aspirate most of the medium from the channels and reservoirs for washing.
Add fresh medium to one of the reservoirs.
Allow the medium to flow through the channel to the other side's reservoir.
Repeat this procedure once more.
Do not remove all medium from the reservoirs during washing.
Reconstitute bEnd5 cell culture as described in the materials and equipment.
Dissociate the cells using trypsin.
Resuspend the pellet in IVC2 medium at a concentration of 10 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Aspirate approximately ¾ of the medium from the reservoirs.
Pipette 80 μL of the endothelial cell suspension into one of the reservoirs of each channel.
Observe the endothelial cells flowing through the channels into the opposing reservoir to monitor the cell seeding.
Once the cells pass through the channel, add 80 μL of cell suspension into each reservoir.
Incubate the device at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 90 min.
Aspirate approximately ¾ of the endothelial cell suspension from the reservoirs.
Add fresh cell suspension, repeating step 11.
Invert the dish with the attached device so that the cells settle by gravity and adhere to the opposite half of the channel wall during the 90 min incubation.
Remove approximately ¾ of the medium containing the endothelial cells from the reservoirs.
Add fresh IVC2 medium.
Incubate the device for 30 min at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Scrape off the layer of endothelial cells in the reservoirs using a P10 pipette tip after the incubation.
Remove the medium containing the scraped cells.
Add fresh medium to the reservoirs and let the medium flow through the channels to wash unattached endothelial cells.
Repeat the process one more time to remove any unattached endothelial cells from the channels and the reservoirs.
Do not remove the medium completely from the reservoirs to prevent fluid depletion in the channels causing them to close.
Add fresh IVC2 medium to the reservoirs.
Place the PDMS-coated plate containing the device on a rocker inside a cell culture incubator (BenchRocker, 30° tilt angle and 12 rpm rocking speed).
Incubate the device on the rocker at 37°C, 5% CO2 overnight.
Add fresh medium in the morning.
Place wet paper on the side of the Petri dish to prevent medium evaporation.
Co-culture the endothelial cells with embryos in an incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for the next 3 days.
Exchange the medium every 36 hours during co-culture.
Alternatively, place the device on a heated microscope stage inside an environmental chamber at 37°C, 5% CO2 for live imaging.
